name: Melat Kiros

summary.text: Melat Kiros is an attorney, a PhD student, and a former barista who is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 1st Congressional District; she identifies as a democratic socialist.

She immigrated to Denver from Tigray, Ethiopia with her family in 1998, earned bachelor's degrees in political science and economics from Washington College in 2018, and a law degree from the University of Notre Dame in 2022.
She defeated 15-term incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette and Wanda James in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, 53.2% to 39.8% to 7.0%.

experience.text: Attorney; was a litigation associate at the law firm Sidley Austin until she says she was fired for defending students' rights to protest.
Worked as a tipped-wage barista at Whittier Cafe in Denver; is currently a PhD student.

research_notes: Verified the secondary-source claim that she defeated Rep. Diana DeGette: confirmed via certified June 30, 2026 primary results on Ballotpedia (Kiros 53.2%, DeGette 39.8%, Wanda James 7.0%). Her campaign site (kirosforco.com) renders as a single-page app in this session's curl fetches, so issue-page quotes were taken from Ballotpedia's verbatim block-quote of that same site (dated April 24, 2026) rather than directly; the underlying site was independently confirmed to exist and match these themes. The Colorado Sun's May 29, 2026 Democratic primary issue guide and the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 candidate Q&A independently corroborate her ICE/immigration position and supplied the federal-budget-law and public-lands quotes. No statement found on tariffs, so that is left unsourced rather than inferred. Second pass 2026-10-14: added housing-state-zoning from https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/10/02/kiros-blau-peterson-congressional-district-1/.
